## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels on this repository; suggested: `orig-external`, `cat-enhancements`, `area:sparse_attention`, `mod-frost`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

The experimental JAX block sparse attention (`cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention`, `cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_{forward,backward}_jax`) ran only on compute capability 10.0. The torch BSA path already serves the same blk128 kernels on cc 10.3.

Admitting cc 10.3 at the device check alone is not enough. `forward_call` and `backward_call` compiled with `compile_options="--gpu-arch=sm_100a"`, and that cubin does not load on cc 10.3: the first run on a B300 with only the check widened failed in both parity cases with `Failed to load cutlass_call function: CuteDSLRT_Error_CudaError`. This PR:

- `jax_api.py`: `is_sm100` accepts compute capability 10.0 or 10.3. `configuration()` keeps the matched device and stores its arch-specific target in `Config.gpu_arch`: `sm_100a` on cc 10.0, `sm_103a` on cc 10.3. Both calls compile with `--gpu-arch={c.gpu_arch}`. `Config` is the `lru_cache` key of both calls, so the two targets never share a compiled call.
- `test/python/block_sparse_attention/jax/conftest.py`, `test_bsa_jax.py`, `cutedsl/test_BSA_jax_parity.py`: accept both parts. The torch-free isolation script checks that device 0 is the default device, not that it is cc 10.0.
- `docs/operations/sparse_attention/bsa.md`: the JAX section's device row says SM100 or SM103.

`test/python/core/jax/conftest.py`, which gates the other JAX suites to cc 10.0, is unchanged.

## Why

On a B300 the JAX API raised "requires ... an SM100 (compute capability 10.0) GPU" although its kernels serve that part through the torch API.

## Related issues

None found.

## API and compatibility impact

None on cc 10.0, which still compiles for `sm_100a`. On cc 10.3 the JAX calls now run instead of raising `ValueError`.

## Testing

B300 (cc 10.3), develop `64ed3dfe` with its own extension, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, JAX 0.12.0.1 (`jax[cuda13]`), `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false`, run from `test/python`:

| Command | develop | check widened only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest block_sparse_attention/jax/test_bsa_jax.py block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_jax_parity.py` | 1 passed, 35 skipped | 2 failed (the parity cases, cubin load), 2 passed, 32 skipped (the JAX conftest still required cc 10.0) | 35 passed, 1 skipped |

The case skipped with this PR needs a process with more than one visible GPU. Not run on cc 10.0.

Thank you for your contribution! Selecting an architecture-specific target and including it in Config addresses the single-device SM103 load problem. The existing SM100 route passed the focused suite. I found one nonblocking issue for JIT calls on a host exposing both architectures.

**[P2] Select the traced call's actual target on mixed SM100/SM103 hosts** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/6266b7f4843a1f99bfbf05f21cc6df778dbb89e4/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/jax_api.py#L120))

With both SM100 and SM103 visible, JIT arguments are tracers, so placed is empty and this selects the first supported local device regardless of where the input arrays are committed. ## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

The experimental JAX block sparse attention (`cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention`, `cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_{forward,backward}_jax`) ran only on compute capability 10.0. The torch BSA path already serves the same blk128 kernels on cc 10.3.

Admitting cc 10.3 at the device check alone is not enough. `forward_call` and `backward_call` compiled with `compile_options="--gpu-arch=sm_100a"`, and that cubin does not load on cc 10.3: the first run on a B300 with only the check widened failed in both parity cases with `Failed to load cutlass_call function: CuteDSLRT_Error_CudaError`. This PR:

- `jax_api.py`: `is_sm100` accepts compute capability 10.0 or 10.3. `configuration()` keeps the matched device and stores its arch-specific target in `Config.gpu_arch`: `sm_100a` on cc 10.0, `sm_103a` on cc 10.3. Both calls compile with `--gpu-arch={c.gpu_arch}`. `Config` is the `lru_cache` key of both calls, so the two targets never share a compiled call.
- `test/python/block_sparse_attention/jax/conftest.py`, `test_bsa_jax.py`, `cutedsl/test_BSA_jax_parity.py`: accept both parts. The torch-free isolation script checks that device 0 is the default device, not that it is cc 10.0.
- `docs/operations/sparse_attention/bsa.md`: the JAX section's device row says SM100 or SM103.

`test/python/core/jax/conftest.py`, which gates the other JAX suites to cc 10.0, is unchanged.

## Why

On a B300 the JAX API raised "requires ... an SM100 (compute capability 10.0) GPU" although its kernels serve that part through the torch API.

## Related issues

None found.

## API and compatibility impact

None on cc 10.0, which still compiles for `sm_100a`. On cc 10.3 the JAX calls now run instead of raising `ValueError`.

## Testing

B300 (cc 10.3), develop `64ed3dfe` with its own extension, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, JAX 0.12.0.1 (`jax[cuda13]`), `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false`, run from `test/python`:

The case skipped with this PR needs a process with more than one visible GPU. Not run on cc 10.0.

Thank you for your contribution! Selecting an architecture-specific target and including it in Config addresses the single-device SM103 load problem. The existing SM100 route passed the focused suite. I found one nonblocking issue for JIT calls on a host exposing both architectures.

**[P2] Select the traced call's actual target on mixed SM100/SM103 hosts** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/6266b7f4843a1f99bfbf05f21cc6df778dbb89e4/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/jax_api.py#L120))

With both SM100 and SM103 visible, JIT arguments are tracers, so placed is empty and this selects the first supported local device regardless of where the input arrays are committed. For example, SM100 arrays with an SM103 first in the device list get sm_100a eagerly but sm_103a under tracing; both call builders then use that wrong architecture-specific target. The reverse ordering breaks the new SM103 route. Choose the target from the actual lowering/execution device, or explicitly reject and document ambiguous mixed-architecture tracing until it is supported. Add a regression using the non-default device in both device orders. This is a narrow, visible load failure; exposing only the intended GPU is a workaround.

Evidence: A probe using real JAX tracers and actual SM100 arrays, with a modeled heterogeneous local_devices list, selected sm_103a during tracing and sm_100a eagerly. Reversing enumeration restored sm_100a. Source lines 133,146,176 pass this selection through to the compiler unchanged. No incompatible binary was launched. Attribution: Introduced by using the first local supported device to choose the new architecture field. The previous fixed sm_100a target still served SM100 arrays in this device ordering.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100 run: 35 passed, 1 skipped across the JAX BSA suite and Torch parity suite. This covers forward, explicit backward, gradients, both layouts, D64/D128, variable counts, asynchronous calls, lowering, and runtime import isolation. The skipped case requires more than one visible GPU. The test runner asserted the exact Python source and compatible reused native binding. Environment: JAX 0.11.0, CuTe DSL 4.8.0, cuDNN 9.20. The mixed-target probe checks real tracing behavior with modeled device enumeration; its result is distinct from native multi-GPU execution. Precheck found no candidates and git diff --check passed. The compiler options reach the existing JAX bridge, and Config separates the two target cache keys. No kernel arithmetic or synchronization changes.
